page: Microsoft Azure D4as_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dav6 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server features 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable for external disk attachments.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25%. Multi-core performance, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core metrics, falls within the average range. However, memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, with both small-block cached and large-block uncached read-only bandwidth testing in the bottom 25%. Cryptographic and integer operations perform moderately, supported by hardware flags such as AVX-512, AES, and SHA_NI.

Given its balanced resource allocation and dedicated CPU model, the D4as_v6 offers a cost-efficient entry point for general-purpose workloads that require consistent CPU performance without massive memory or local storage requirements. It is well-suited for static web serving, text processing, and lightweight application hosting. It is less optimal for memory-intensive databases, software compilation, or large-scale LLM inference due to weaker memory bandwidth and lower multi-threaded decompression speeds.
